title: How far is any point of the circle from P?
description: A circle is drawn with the compass tip on P and the pencil four centimetres from the tip. The video asks how far a point on the circle is from P, and gives the names centre and radius. Keeko raises the doubt that a point on the far side is more than four centimetres away.
teaching_notes: One idea: every point of a circle is the same distance from its centre, and that distance is the radius. Watch for children who think the far side of the circle is further from the centre.

source: Take a point on the circle. What will be its distance from P: equal to 4 cm, less than 4 cm or greater than 4 cm?
video_script.why: The child sees that the pencil stayed four centimetres from the tip, so every point of the circle is four centimetres from P.
video_script.substitution: Lay a ruler from P to points on different sides of the circle.
video_script.anchor: The circle drawn with the compass tip on P
video_script.wrong_answer: the point on the far side is more than four centimetres from P
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a point on the far side of the circle is further from P. A ruler laid from P to that point reads four centimetres.
video_script.payoff_line: The distance is equal to four centimetres, for every point on the circle.

final_answer.value: equal to 4 cm for every point; P is the centre and the distance is the radius
final_answer.spoken: equal to four centimetres for every point on the circle; P is the centre and the distance is the radius

never_show: a point inside or outside the circle
maths_rules: The pencil stays 4 cm from the tip, and the tip stays on P.
Every point of the circle is 4 cm from P: equal to 4 cm, not less and not more.
The centre is P; the radius is the fixed distance, 4 cm.
video_script.design: One idea: all points of a circle are at one distance from its centre. Assumes the circle drawn with the compass. Wrong idea: the far side is further. The circle stays all video.
